segments.he: לְאֵיתוֹיֵי שְׁבָחָא דְּמִמֵּילָא: חֲפוּרָה וַהֲווֹ שׁוּבְלֵי, שַׁלְפּוּפֵי וַהֲווֹ תַּמְרֵי.
segments.en: The Gemara explains that this halakha is repeated in order «to include an enhancement that» occurs «by itself» after the death of the father or husband, for instance in a case when «fodder [ḥafura],» i.e., produce that has grown stalks but is not yet ripe, «becomes full ears,» or when «date flowers [shalpufei] become» fully developed «dates.» Despite the fact that in such cases the property became enhanced by itself, without any effort on the part of the other brothers, the firstborn may not claim his double portion from that enhancement, and the same applies in the other cases mentioned in the mishna.

moves.summary: the repetition includes natural enhancement (grain ripening, dates)
